title: Can you find the Pink Elephant hiding in this image?
author: Find_Bono
selftext:
This is one of the images in my new daily game Find Bono. Race to find Bono the elephant in a new packed environment every day. I'm quite happy with the image results I've gotten so far and I am optimistic that they will continue to improve. 

You can play for free at: [https://findbono.com/](https://findbono.com/)

comments.author: Itchy-Individual3536
comments.body: Problem with these images is that zoomed out they look very convincing, but when you zoom in, everything is just smudged rubbish. It destroys the fun aspect of hidden picture puzzles if you can't find any fun little scene during the hunt.

replies.author: Find_Bono
replies.body: yes that's what I meant with improvements in the future

replies.author: Thomas-Lore
replies.body: It is not that hard to avoid - generate it in small parts and combine in GIMP on layers. This is what I have done for my point&click adventure (Aether Collector) to have looong screens you can walk on.

replies.author: Find_Bono
replies.body: What do you mean by that exactly? I do generate the actual targets separately and edit them in right now. But I wouldn't know how to generate the background in parts so that you can still edit them together.

replies.author: Thomas-Lore
replies.body:
It is not easy to explain and it depends on what tools you are using. But for example if you are using local models what you could try is cut the background image into even pieces and regenerate each piece at full resolution (using image to image), then combine them back in GIMP/Photoshop fixing any issues on where the edges connect by hand. 

If you are using MJ you could use their new editor for something similar (upload the pieces, describe then and use retexture so it regenerates them).
